title: Kepler Sun-like stars with a co-moving Gaia companion inside the aperture show 3.5 times more superflares; Gaia DR2 lists most such companions, so only unresolved ones can bias localised rates
abstract: Question: do faint companions cause part of the Kepler superflares of Sun-like stars, as a campaign TESS study found, and can they bias the once-per-century rate of Vasilyev et al. (2024)? Approach: the Vasilyev et al. star and flare lists were not accessible (HTTP 403), so we rebuilt their sample (45,741 Kepler stars, Teff 5000-6500 K, 4 < M_G < 6, RUWE < 1.4, no period below 20 d) and used the Yang & Liu (2019) and Davenport (2016) flare catalogues, Gaia DR3 neighbours within 15 arcsec with a shuffle test for chance pairs, Kepler pixel difference images with injection tests, and Gaia DR2 counterparts. Findings: stars with a co-moving companion within 6 arcsec have a flare of 1e34 erg or more 3.5 times more often (95% 2.4-5.0; odds ratio 3.4 with covariates); companions at 8-15 arcsec give no excess (1.01). Kepler pixels put 19 of 59 measured flares (11 of 27 stars) on the companion and 0 of 39 control flares on a fake position (p = 3e-5). Gaia DR2 lists 91-99 percent of these companions, and the 2022 catalogue of the Vasilyev et al. localisation code shows fewer companions among target-assigned flare stars (2.3 percent against 6.1 percent), so the localisation removes resolved-companion flares. RUWE 1.2-1.4 (ratio 3.2) and Gaia IPD multi-peak flags (3.4) show that unresolved pairs also flare more; if companions at 10 au to 1 arcsec flare like resolved ones, they explain about 45 percent (23-69) of the flaring stars of an unlocalised catalogue. Limitations: no direct test of the Vasilyev et al. lists; other flare thresholds (the Yang & Liu flaring stars mostly flare many times); 56 percent purity of the co-moving class; the unresolved budget is a scenario.

display.caption: Superflare incidence ratio of Kepler Sun-like stars by Gaia DR3 neighbour class (Yang & Liu 2019 flares; 95% intervals). Co-moving companions inside 6 arcsec raise the incidence; companions at 8-15 arcsec do not.
Fraction of stars with a flare of at least 1e34 erg against the separation of the nearest co-moving Gaia DR3 companion. The excess stops near the size of the Kepler apertures.

Kepler pixel test. Left: companion share of each flare difference image for stars with a co-moving companion at 1-6 arcsec and for control stars. Right: quiet and flare images of KIC 4756335; the flare light falls on the companion.

citations.reason: TESS study that found companion-driven superflares; it left the Kepler sample untested. We test Kepler and reuse its idea of offset direction toward the companion.
